title: Private VPC: Offline Patch Orchestration & Network Policy DSL PRD
creator: Sofia Martinez
description: PRD for a combined Offline Patch Orchestration workflow and a declarative Network Policy DSL for Private/VPC Redwood deployments. Goal: enable customers operating in sealed or limited-egress environments to stage, validate, and safely apply OS/container/runtime patches and agent upgrades with minimal live-operator intervention while preserving strict egress constraints and auditable artifact provenance.
context_and_background: Customers in regulated environments require predictable, auditable upgrade paths that do not rely on continuous outbound connectivity. Existing private-deploy upgrade work focuses on image mirroring and staged rollouts; this PRD defines an orchestration layer plus a compact policy DSL to codify acceptable egress allowances, artifact sourcing, staging windows, and rollback semantics.
goals: Allow fully offline patch orchestration using pre-fetched signed artifact bundles (mirrors or physical media)
Provide a declarative Network Policy DSL to express minimal temporary egress (egress exceptions) needed for orchestration verification and health checks
Ensure strong artifact provenance: checksums, signature verification, and KMS/HSM key rotation support
Support staged rollouts (canary -> cohort -> full), automatic rollback on health regressions, and operator override
Emit detailed audit logs and telemetry for compliance and postmortem analysis
out_of_scope: Automatic external package ingestion (customers must provide mirrors or signed bundles)
Full implementation of operator-based chaos tests (we will provide hooks but not run chaos by default)
acceptance_criteria: Offline Orchestration: Customer can deliver a signed artifact bundle (tar+manifest) to an airgapped cluster and trigger a patch run without any outbound connections to Redwood control plane
Policy DSL: Customer can declare an egress exception policy via the DSL (max 1 IP, port, and 2-hour window) and the system enforces activation/deactivation with operator confirmation
Provenance: All applied bundles must be verified against embedded checksums and a PKI-signed manifest; mismatches reject the bundle and record an audit entry

Staged Rollout: System supports canary cohort (configurable size), monitors health metrics (latency, error rate, pod restarts) for a configurable watch window, and auto-rolls-back on threshold violations
Rollback Guarantee: Rollback path exists and can be initiated automatically or by operator; post-rollback validation runs succeed in 95% of simulated rollback tests

Audit & Telemetry: Each step (bundle validation, stage start/complete/fail, egress activation/deactivation, signature verification) is logged with a UUID and stored in the customer-visible audit store for at least 90 days
Operator Safety: Any automated egress policy activation requires either (a) pre-approved DSL policy with a signed consent token, or (b) explicit operator approval recorded in audit logs

KMS Integration: Support for rotating signing keys and verifying bundle signatures against a configurable KMS/HSM endpoint; key rotation does not block previously-signed approved bundles until expiry date in manifest
security_considerations: Ensure manifest signature verification occurs in a hardened execution path separate from the unpacking logic
Egress DSL must include safe-defaults to prevent accidental wide-open windows (deny-by-default)
Operator approval flows must be tamper-evident and replay-resistant (nonce + timestamp + signature)
Minimize sensitive secrets in operator UIs; use short-lived tokens for egress activation
solution_approach: Design a lightweight Network Policy DSL (YAML) with primitives: allow-egress {ip|cidr}, port-range, duration, purpose-tag
Build an orchestration controller that validates bundle signatures, runs pre-flight checks, stages artifacts to a local mirror, and executes patch playbooks via the existing operator
Integrate with existing mirror tooling (S3 compatible endpoint) and add checksum/signature verification step in the operator bootstrap
Add a bounded egress activation mechanism: K8s admission + operator that programs temporary cluster egress via a validated firewall/egress-proxy configuration and auto-reverts after the duration
Telemetry hooks: emit structured events to the on-prem telemetry sink and to the Redwood console when connectivity exists; include correlation IDs for end-to-end traceability
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Mis-declared DSL could allow excessive egress. Mitigation: deny-by-default, validation rules, and operator approval gating
Risk: Signature verification complexity across KMS providers. Mitigation: define a minimal signing spec and provide reference tooling for common KMS providers (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, HashiCorp Vault)
Risk: Rollback failure due to stateful services. Mitigation: require per-service pre-check scripts and include snapshot hints in the manifest where supported
operational_playbook: Step 1: Customer uploads signed bundle to mirror or provides physical media and registers bundle manifest in the operator
Step 2: Operator runs preflight - verifies signatures, disk space, and required Kubernetes API access
Step 3: If DSL egress activation required, display consent screen and require operator signature; system programs temporary egress and starts timer
Step 4: Execute canary cohort, monitor configured health metrics; if pass, continue to next cohort; if fail, trigger rollback and escalate
Step 5: On completion, revoke temporary egress, store full audit record, and surface result in the Console and in customer logs
metrics_and_slos: Rollback success rate >= 95% in internal tests
Operator egress activation must not exceed declared duration by more than 10s
implementation_notes: Prefer building the DSL parser in Go and reuse existing operator SDK
Create a conformance test-suite that runs against sealed clusters to validate DSL enforcement and offline-run behavior
Expose a dry-run mode that simulates orchestration without applying changes for operator sign-off
